method: Every Commons file was opened through the Commons API (action=query&prop=imageinfo|revisions, extmetadata + full wikitext). archive.org items were checked through archive.org/metadata/<id>. Rule applied: named human performer; the RECORDING's license must be PD, CC0, CC BY or CC BY-SA and valid in the US; historic transfers only if recorded and issued before 1926.

picks.why: No recording I could find is both by a named performer and free in the US. Commons has only the Barbirolli/Halle 1947 transfer (PD-EU-audio; US-protected). archive.org has Barbirolli 1947/1962, BBC SO/Boult, Toscanini 1951, Monteux 1958, Bernstein 1982, A. Davis 1991 with no license; the only CC-tagged item (Kirchenkonzert Marienborn 2012) is CC BY-NC-ND. US Marine Band (Patterson transcription, 26 Aug 2021) has no released download; US Army Field Band's track has spoken narration over it and is a commercial Altissimo release.
picks.lead: Elgar's own acoustic recording (Royal Albert Hall Orchestra, HMV, Nimrod cut Feb 1920) and Henry Wood/New Queen's Hall Orchestra (Columbia, 1924) are pre-1926 and so PD in the US, but I found no free, licensed transfer online (only commercial remasters: SOMM Ariadne 5046, Pristine PASC313). Nimrod is heavily abridged in the 1920 set. Elgar's 1926 electrical remake becomes US-PD on 2027-01-01 only if published in 1926.

spot_check.file: File:Clair de lune (Claude Debussy) Suite bergamasque.ogg
spot_check.license_on_page: Recording CC BY 3.0 ({{Copyright information|recording={{cc-by-3.0}}}}); composition PD
spot_check.verdict: KEEP, but fix the credit. audio/music/CREDITS.md and docs/music/REVIEW.md say 'Public domain' / 'PD mark'. The recording is CC BY 3.0, so it needs attribution (the extmetadata LicenseShortName shows 'Public domain' because the composition template comes first). Credit: 'Laurens Goedhart, CC BY 3.0'.

spot_check.file: File:Nocturne Op. 9 no. 2 in E flat major.mp3
spot_check.real_performer: not named: the Commons page credits only Chopin and Musopen (source archive.org/details/musopen-chopin, creator 'Aaron Dunn', the Musopen founder). The file has no artist tag there either
spot_check.verdict: LICENSE OK, PERFORMER UNNAMED. It sounds like a real piano recording (Musopen's Chopin project), but it doesn't meet the 'named human performer' bar as written. Keep it if Claude accepts 'Musopen' as the performer credit, as for the Grieg and Mozart picks; otherwise replace.
